t3054.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records ʿĀṣim b. Bahdala, i.e. Ibn Abī al-Najūd, al-Asadī, their client, al-Kūfī, Abū Bakr the reciter, as truthful but with illusions, an authority in recitation, his hadith in the two Ṣaḥīḥs as supporting; of the sixth generation, died in the year 28.
as: صدوق له أوهام حجة في القراءة وحديثه في الصحيحين مقرون
Truthful but has illusions; an authority in recitation, and his hadith is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs as a supporting narration.
وكان ثقة، إلا أنه كان كثير الخطأ في حديثه
He was reliable, but made many errors in hadith.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان رجلا صالحا قارئا للقرآن، وأهل الكوفة يختارون قراءته وأنا أختار قراءته، وكان خيرا ثقة، والأعمش أحفظ منه، وكان شعبة يختار الأعمش عليه، في تثبيت الحديث
A righteous man and Qurʾān reciter. Kūfans preferred his reading, as do I. He was good and reliable, though al-Aʿmash had better retention, and Shuʿbah preferred al-Aʿmash in establishing hadith.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
There is no objection to him.
عاصم صاحب سنة وقراءة للقرآن، وكان ثقة، رأسا في القراءة، ويقال: إن الأعمش قرأ عليه وهو حدث، وكان يختلف عليه في زر وأبي وائل

ʿĀṣim adhered to the Sunnah and recited the Qurʾān. He was reliable and a leading authority in recitation. Al-Aʿmash reportedly read under him when young, and transmissions through ʿĀṣim differed over Zirr and Abū Wāʾil.
يعقوب بن سفيان, quoted by al-Mizzī
His hadith contains inconsistencies, though he is reliable.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
محله عندي محل الصدق، صالح الحديث، ولم يكن بذاك الحافظ
In my view he ranks as truthful. His hadith is acceptable, though his retention was not outstanding.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان كل من كان اسمه عاصم، سئ الحفظ
Everyone called ʿĀṣim was poor at retaining hadith.
There is no objection to him.
There is objectionable material in his hadith.
أبو جعفر العقيلي, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم يكن فيه إلا سوء الحفظ
His only failing was poor retention.
There are reservations about his retention.
وكان عاصم ثقة إلا أنه كان كثير الخطأ في حديثه
ʿĀṣim was reliable, though he made many mistakes in his hadith.

t6725.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Muʿādh ibn Jabal ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, as a well-known foremost Companion who witnessed Badr and later battles, with the utmost knowledge of legal rulings and the Qur'an. He died in Syria in 18.
as: The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by al-Mizzī
وأعلمهم بالحلال والحرام معاذ بن جبل
Muʿādh ibn Jabal was the most knowledgeable among them about what is lawful and unlawful.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by al-Mizzī
Muʿādh ibn Jabal is an excellent man.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by al-Mizzī
Muʿādh, by God, I love you.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by al-Mizzī
يأتي معاذ بن جبل يوم القيامة أمام العلماء يرثوه.
Muʿādh comes a short distance ahead of the scholars on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Mizzī calls this version mursal.
وكذلك كان معاذ كان يعلم الناس الخير وكان مطيعا لله ولرسوله.
Muʿādh used to teach people goodness and obeyed God and His Messenger.
عجزت النساء أن يلدن مثل معاذ لولا معاذ هلك عمر.
Women have been unable to bear anyone like Muʿādh. Without him ʿUmar would have perished.
He was one of the most eminent people.
We used to compare him with Abraham.
His merits and virtues were very many.
الإمام المقدم في علم الحلال والحرام
The foremost authority on lawful and unlawful matters.
كعب بن مالك, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
كان شابا جميلا سمحا من خير شباب قومه.
He was handsome and generous, among the best young men of his people.
Abū Nuʿaym, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
إمام الفقهاء، وكنز العلماء، شهد العقبة، وبدرا، والمشاهد، وكان من أفضل شباب الأنصار حلما وحياء وسخاء
A leader of jurists and a treasure among scholars. He attended al-ʿAqabah, Badr and the campaigns and was among the best young Anṣār in forbearance, modesty and generosity.
ابن كعب بن مالك, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
كان معاذ شابا جميلا سمحا لا يسأل الله شيئا إلا أعطاه.
Muʿādh was handsome and generous, and God granted him whatever he asked.
عمر, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
عجزت النساء أن يلدن مثل معاذ، ولولا معاذ لهلك عمر.
Women have been unable to bear anyone like Muʿādh. Without him ʿUmar would have perished.
النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
Muʿādh was the most knowledgeable among them about what is lawful and unlawful.
النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
يأتي معاذ يوم القيامة أمام الناس برتوة
Muʿādh will come a short distance ahead of the people on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Ḥajar calls this report mursal.
النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
I have sent you the best of my people. Ibn Ḥajar says its chain is interrupted.
ابن مسعود, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
ما نسيت، إنا كنا نشبهه بإبراهيم عليه السلام.
I did not forget. We used to liken him to Abraham.
Abū Nuʿaym, quoted by Ibn Ḥajar al-ʿAsqalānī
وكان من أفضل شباب الأنصار حلما وحياء وسخاء
He was among the best young men of the Anṣār for forbearance, modesty and generosity.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
أعلمهم بالحلال والحرام معاذ بن جبل.
Muʿādh ibn Jabal was the most knowledgeable among them on what is lawful and unlawful.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
يأتي معاذ بن جبل يوم القيامة أمام العلماء.
Muʿādh will come ahead of the scholars on the Day of Resurrection.
عبد الله بن عمر, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
هما معاذ بن جبل، وأبو الدرداء.
He calls Muʿādh and Abū al-Dardāʾ the two discerning men.
ابن مسعود, quoted by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr
وكذلك كان معاذ بن جبل معلما للخير مطيعا لله ولرسوله.
Muʿādh taught goodness and obeyed God and His Messenger.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
وأعلمهم بالحلال والحرام معاذ بن جبل
Muʿādh was the most knowledgeable among them in lawful and unlawful matters.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
صدق معاذ. صدق معاذ. صدق معاذ.
Muʿādh spoke the truth, repeated three times about the report he had transmitted.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
معاذ أمام العلماء يوم القيامة برتوة أو رتوتين.
Muʿādh will be a short distance or two ahead of the scholars on the Day of Resurrection.
جابر بن عبد الله, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
كان معاذ بن جبل من أحسن الناس وجها، وأحسنه خلقا، وأسمحه كفا
He was among the most handsome, best in character and most generous of people.
ابن مسعود, quoted by Ibn al-Athīr
وكذلك كان معاذ معلما للخير، مطيعا لله عز وجل ولرسوله
He taught goodness and obeyed God and His Messenger.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
أعلم أمتي بالحلال والحرام معاذ بن جبل
Muʿādh was the most knowledgeable in my community in what is lawful and unlawful.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
إني قد بعثت عليكم من خير أهلي والي علمهم والي دينهم.
I have sent you one of the best of my people, entrusted with their knowledge and religion.
جابر بن عبد الله, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
كان معاذ بن جبل. رحمه الله. من أحسن الناس وجها وأحسنه خلقا وأسمحه كفا
Muʿādh was among the most handsome, best in character and most generous of people.
إن العلماء إذا اجتمعوا يوم القيامة كان معاذ بن جبل بين أيديهم قذفة حجر
When the scholars assemble at the Resurrection, Muʿādh will be a stone’s throw ahead of them. ʿUmar attributes these words to the Prophet.
The Prophet ﷺ, quoted by Ibn Saʿd
أعلم أمتي بالحلال والحرام معاذ بن جبل
Muʿādh was the most knowledgeable in my community in what is lawful and unlawful.

t7072.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim al-Nawfalī, Abū Muḥammad and Abū ʿAbd Allāh, a Medinan, as trustworthy and virtuous, from the third generation, who died in 99 AH.
as: وكان ثقة أكثر حديثا من أخيه
Al-Wāqidī: trustworthy, with more hadith than his brother.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
وقال في موضع أخر: أحد الأئمة
Ibn Khirāsh elsewhere: one of the imams.
كان من خيار الناس، كان يحج ماشيا وناقته تقاد، وكان يخضب بالوسمة
Ibn Ḥibbān: one of the best of people; he made Hajj on foot with his camel led, and dyed with wasmah.
كان يعد فصحاء قريش هؤلاء الثلاثة: عمر بن عبد العزيز، وسليمان بن عبد الملك، ونافع ابن جبير
The most eloquent of Quraysh were counted as three: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik and Nāfiʿ ibn Jubayr.

t7256.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Hashim ibn al-Qasim ibn Muslim al-Laythi al-Baghdadi, Abu al-Nadr, known by his kunya and nicknamed Qaysar, as trustworthy and firmly established, of the ninth generation, who died in 207 at age seventy-three.
as: Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو النضر شيخنا من الآمرين بالمعروف والناهين عن المنكر
Aḥmad: Abū al-Naḍr, our shaykh, is among those who enjoin good and forbid evil.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Aḥmad: Abū al-Naḍr is among the careful, exacting narrators of Baghdad.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Aḥmad: Abū al-Naḍr is more reliable than Shādhān.
أحمد بن منصور الرمادي, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو النضر أثبت من وهب بن جرير
al-Ramādī: Abū al-Naḍr is more reliable than Wahb ibn Jarīr.
محمد ابن مسلم بن وارة, quoted by al-Mizzī
Ibn Wārah (disagreeing): Wahb ibn Jarīr is more reliable.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو النضر من الأبناء، سكن بغداد، ثقة صاحب سنة، وكان أهل بغداد يفخرون به
al-ʿIjlī: Abū al-Naḍr, of the Abnāʾ, lived in Baghdad, trustworthy, a man of Sunnah; the people of Baghdad took pride in him.
أحمد بن حبنل, quoted by al-Mizzī
أبو النضر كتب عن شعبة إملاء
Aḥmad: Abū al-Naḍr wrote from Shuʿbah by dictation.
ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī, quoted by al-Mizzī
وكذلك قال علي ابن المديني ، ومحمد بن سعد ، أبو حاتم

t7911.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd al-Thaqafī, brother of Ziyād on his father's side before Muʿāwiya claimed Ziyād, of the second generation; he is mentioned but has no transmission.

t8002.bio: Ibn Ḥajar reports conflicting names for Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī, calls him a transmitter of historical reports abandoned in hadith, places him in the sixth generation, and gives his death as year 67.
as: a transmitter of historical reports, abandoned in hadith

t8095.bio: Ibn Ḥajar says Abū Rajāʾ, who transmits from Abū al-Ṣalt, is said to be al-Harawī, otherwise unknown of that generation; Abū Dāwūd cites him.

t8213.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū ʿAbd Allāh as a man who had Companionship and a hadith on fasting, from whom ʿArfaja transmitted.

t8266.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū ʿUmar al-Ṣīnī as acceptable, of the sixth generation; his name is said to be Nashīṭ but that is an error, and his report from Abū al-Dardāʾ is mursal.

t8288.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Shāmī as unknown (majhūl), of the fifth generation.

t8587.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ruqayya bint ʿUmar, also given as ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, described as maqbūla and belonging to the fourth generation.

t8774.bio: Ibn Ḥajar lists Umm Manbūdh, mother of Manbūdh ibn Abī Sulaymān, of the third generation, and grades her acceptable.

t95.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Ṭarsūsī, truthful, of the twelfth generation; Ibn ʿAsākir said he is rather Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar, and Ibn Yūnus mentioned no other.
as: إنما هو محمد بن أحمد بن جعفر
He is rather Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar.

t989.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Juwayriyah ibn Qudāmah al-Tamīmī as trustworthy, of the second generation, a mukhaḍram; it is said he is Jāriyah ibn Qudāmah mentioned earlier.
